proof_summary: The cases \(1\le k\le 59\) are settled by explicit prime decompositions. For \(k\ge 60\), set \(n=2k+1\); if \(4k+2=2n\) were not a sum of two primes, every matrix entry would be zero because its two candidate primes sum to \(2n\), forcing the determinant to vanish and contradicting the hypothesis.
